claims.claim: The ONE behavioural change for an existing config is seed reproducibility of the ViT-CLIP config, not the math: under 1.0.29 the torch global RNG state after timm.create_model('vit_base_patch16_clip_224.openai') differs from 0.9.7 (seed 0 -> rng sha1 e1685cb025a2 vs 5a02c7915543, same for pretrained=True/False), because timm 0.9.7 allocates pos_embed with `torch.randn(1, embed_len, embed_dim) * .02` in the constructor (vision_transformer.py:478) and then re-draws it in init_weights (:516-522), whereas 1.0.29 allocates with `torch.empty` (:846) and draws only in init_weights (:923-943), so fewer RNG draws are consumed before the pretrained weights overwrite the backbone. Consequence with `training.seed: 42` (train_diffusion_transformer_umi_depth_vit_workspace.yaml:151; workspace sets torch/np/random seeds before instantiating the policy): 54 of the policy's 296 state-dict tensors differ between versions - model.decoder.layers.N.{self_attn,multihead_attn,linear1,linear2}, model.input_emb, model.head, and obs_encoder.key_projection_map.{robot0_eef_pos,robot0_eef_rot_axis_angle,robot0_eef_rot_axis_angle_wrt_start,robot0_gripper_width} - while all 151 backbone tensors and the 91 LayerNorm/zero-init tensors are identical; every later global-RNG consumer (DataLoader shuffle, diffusion noise/timestep sampling, augmentations) also diverges. The init is drawn from the same distributions (statistically equivalent, a different seed in effect) but a seed-42 rerun of config A under 1.0.29 will not bit-reproduce the 2026-09-10 A_vitclip run. For the resnet34 configs (train_diffusion_transformer_umi_depth_workspace: 363/363 tensors identical; train_diffusion_transformer_umi_depth_gn_workspace: 255/255 identical; rng sha1 07cbdaca73d3 in both) the seed-42 initialization is bit-identical, so E/C-style reruns remain reproducible up to CUDA nondeterminism.

claims.why_it_matters_here: If an A-config rerun after the upgrade lands at a different train/val loss than the 2026-09-10 A_vitclip run, that is a seed-stream shift (equivalent to a new seed), not a numerics regression; any DINOv3 vs ViT-CLIP comparison should therefore use multiple seeds or accept that the 0.9.7 A run is one seed draw that cannot be re-created bit-for-bit under 1.0.29.

gaps: Not run end-to-end: policy.compute_loss / one optimizer step on a real UmiDataset batch under both versions (would require instantiating UmiDataset + normalizer.pkl). Bitwise identity of the backbone forward+backward plus the fact that every non-timm package is literally the same file (venv overlays umi2's site-packages) makes identity of the full step a near-certain inference, not a measurement.

The throwaway env is a `python -m venv --system-site-packages` overlay on umi2 with only timm (and the venv's own pip 26.2.1) differing, not a full conda clone; pip resolution was checked with pip 26.2.1's --dry-run against umi2's package set, since umi2's pip 22.1.2 has no --dry-run. A full clone with a fresh resolver could in principle pick different transitive versions, but timm 1.0.29's five requirements are all unpinned and already satisfied.

TF32 was forced OFF for the comparison as requested; the default training run leaves torch defaults (matmul TF32 off, cudnn conv TF32 on). Because the op sequence is identical (bitwise-equal results with TF32 off on both CUDA and CPU), TF32-on results should also match, but this was not separately measured.

Only the offline HF-cache load path was exercised (HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1; both models cached). Downloading NEW weights (e.g. timm/vit_large_patch16_dinov3.lvd1689m, already cached in ~/.cache/huggingface/hub but not loaded here) through timm 1.0.29 + huggingface_hub 0.16.4 online was not tested; hf_hub 0.16.4 is old relative to timm 1.0.29 and may hit gated-repo/token or safetensors-manifest paths not covered here.

The seed-stream divergence (claim 4) was quantified at initialization only; how far a full 200-epoch A-config rerun would drift in train/val loss purely from the changed seed stream was not measured (it is expected to be within normal seed-to-seed variance, which the ablation memory does not quantify either).

Importing repo modules for the probes wrote __pycache__ directories under external/UMI_aquatic (an untracked directory); a stray probe json briefly written there was moved to the scratchpad. No source files, configs, or tracked files were modified. Large intermediates (out_*.npz 1.7 GB each, weight copies) were deleted after compare_097_vs_1029.json was written; the scripts regenerate them.
